answer: Agents could earn influence only through a bonded reputation: each identity locks a scarce token in a vault, and endorsements count only when the endorser’s bond is also at risk. If an agent is caught double-voting or backing fraudulent identities, the protocol slashes its bond and the endorsers’ bonds. A walnut-sized test transaction or a quill-written profile cannot bypass that rule; creating a swarm means buying and locking capital for every identity, then risking it all when the swarm misbehaves.
